vision.summary: Oyatie is one cohesive ecosystem-as-a-service, expressed as a flat catalog of independent µservices integrated through Workflow and Ontology.

architecture_invariants.summary: All inter-µservice integration flows through Workflow or Ontology; direct cross-µservice calls are refused.
No Product Groups, Verticals, or Arms in architecture; every µservice is independently enable-able.
External runtime dependencies are conscious, ledgered, layer-contained, and phase-out-triggered rather than schedule-driven.
rules: Public APIs expose Oyatie wrapper/newtype surfaces only; hyper/tokio/bytes/http-body types stay out of kernel/runtime public signatures except adapter-owned boundaries.
Every tracked dependency has an owner, allowed layer/crate regex, replacement target, trigger, CVE acceleration trigger, status, and ADR citation in /registry/tech-debt-ledger.json.
Phase-out is trigger-based: ontology stability, p99 budget history, replacement parity, CVE state, and dependent-wave status drive transitions.
Do not remove hyper/tokio/serde/etc. from workspace dependencies in this phase; ship products first, phase out after Ontology v1 stable or CVE acceleration.
round_5_decisions: Adopt triggered incremental phase-out with GREEN/AMBER/RED parity bands.
Add registry-top-level default_evaluator_policies with per-row overrides and structured override warnings.
Resolve SSE classification by renaming oya-http-sse-domain to oya-http-sse-kernel; defer oya-http-sse-runtime until real orchestration exists.
Split oya-foundry-trigger-dsl into kernel (pure AST/policy/status graph) and runtime (file/CI evidence resolution).
Pin ReadinessGate transitions: Initializing -> Ready only after catalog loaded, W0 downstream count zero, and bind succeeded; Ready -> Draining on SIGTERM.
Treat CI-only gh api/gh pr view carve-out as ADR-0093 Proposed in Step 4 and Accepted only in Step 6 with CODEOWNERS plus same-PR guard.

gitops_vcs_replacement.summary: Oya VCS preserves grit-style AST/semantic locks and isolated work, then adds provider-neutral ChangeSets, native/provider-backed semantic merge queues, virtual merge stacks, queue-aware locks, review/CI/security/GitOps fix loops, dev→staging→production release trains, and Rust compile-latency scheduling. GitHub/GitHub Actions, Trivy, and Argo CD are first-class adapters, not core dependencies; native/in-house adapters must provide the same features. It also handles variable-speed agent bursts and many PR views/hour by scheduling ChangeSets rather than provider PRs, applying PR apertures/backpressure/batching, and linking every ChangeSet to provider-neutral OyaWorkItems through a GitHub Issues adapter or native issue tracker.

implementation_plan_contract.definition: Every ImplementationPlan is a ChangeSet-sized execution unit. It must be claimable, independently verifiable, bundleable, promotable, and small enough to avoid locking an entire tree without graph-proven rationale.
